MAN LEY JAMES CLARKE

This Grand Lodge lost a valuable member when M an ley J. Clarke
of Livermore passed away on January 11, 1960. This loss will be most
keenly felt by Mosaic Lodge No. 218. of which he ·was a Past Master
and in whose affairs he has been so keenly active.
Manley J. Clarke was almost 78 years of age at the time of his death,
having been born in Newark, New York. on February 7, 1882. His
early life was spent in Buffalo, New York. He received his law degree
from Georgetow n University in W ashington , D . C. in 1908. Living
in Livermore for many years. he was raised in M osaic Lodge on April
4, 1922 and served as Master of that Lodge in 1925. He was appointed
Inspector for that Dis trict in 1928 and continued to serve as such until
1943. Until his death. he continued active in the affairs of Mosaic Lodge,
guiding it in all legal matters and often acting as Installing Officer at
its Annual Installa tions.
Manley J. Clarke served as Judge of the Livermore Court from 1930
until 1953 and was a ctive in many communit y affairs. H e will be greatly
missed. not only by his Lodge, but by the communit y he served so
faithfully.
He is survived by his wife in Livermore , to whom our sympathy goes
out, and by a brother livi ng in Oakland.
CARL CURTIS MIKESELL

A Mason beloved by his brethren passed away when the messen ger
of death summoned C arl Curtis M ikesell of Needles on June 20. I 960.
Brother Mike. as he was affectiona tely known to his brethren , was 81
yea rs of age . C arl Mikesell was a long time resident of Needles, having
lived in that City since 1917. U ntil his retirement in 1949 he was in the
employ o f the Santa Fe Railway and a member of the Brotherhood of
Locomotiv e Firemen and Engineme n. A s a Mason he was in labors
most abundant. He was raised in Needles Lodge No. 326 on January 26.
I 920 and served as M aster of that Lodge in 1924. 1925. and 1927. H e
was elected Secretary of the Lodge in I 927 <1nd for the past thirty-thre e
years has continued to serve in that office. H e was appointed Inspector
of District No. 601 in 1935 and held that pos ition till 1957 - for twentytwo years. H e was a member of York R ite Masonry, being the first
High Priest of Havasu Chapter No. 148 R.A.M. and a member of S t.
Bernard Command ery No. 23. H e was also a member of Al M alaikah
Shrine and of Needles Chapter of the Eastern Star. For twen ty-five
years he was Associate Guardian of Bethel N o. I 05 Order of Job's
Daughters . He was also a n active member of the M ethodist Church of
N eedles and of the Senior C itizens' Club of that City.
With a record of service such as that compiled by Mike Mikesell.
we can appreciate the words of Officers of his Lodge who w rote. " This

was a great loss to us , for he was not only our Secretary, but a personal

servant. Enter into the joy o f thy Lord."

great tenets of Brotherly Love, Relief. and Truth.

DECISION NO. 2
D ecision No. 2 held that the Chaplain of a Lodge must be a member
of the Lodge. Section 473 o f the Masonic Code specifies that members
of the Lodge are eligible for elective office, and we feel that it is the
intention of our law that only members of the Lodge are eligible for
appointive office. We concur with the Grand Master.
Adopted.

DECISION NO. 8
Decision No. 8 holds tha t an applicant who was convicted of a
felony . served time in prison and was unconditionally pardoned, is
ineligible to receive the degrees of Masonry. Section 51 1-h of the
Masonic Code states that the test is whether or not the applicant has
served a time of imprisonment in a sta te or federal prison, and, applying
this test, we concur with the Grand Master. (Not to be recorded in the
Code.)
A dopted.

DECISION NO. 12
DECISION NO. 4

Decision No. 4 held that a Board of Trustees of a Lodge may not
dispose of Lodge funds or property without the approval of the Lodge.
Section 409 of the M asonic Code provides that Lodge funds are trust
funds, and Section 405 provides that Lodge trustees shall always be
under the control of the Lodge and shall sell, invest, etc., the funds as
the Lodge shall direct. These s ections specifically require Lodge action
and we concur with the Grand Master . (Not to be recorded in the
Code).
Adopted.

such requests were improper and should not be acceded to without
special a uthority from the Grand Master. Every Lodge is expected
to meet its opera ting expenses from the income of dues. The Trustees
of a Temple Association are charged with careful conservation of the

There was referred to your C ommittee on Ju risprudence the question:
May printed or written invitations be sent to the brethren to attend
the conferring o f a degree upon a named candidate?
Sec. 518-a and b, C.M.C.. provides that the names of candidates to
receive degree work cannot be printed on cards or posted on bulletin
boards.
We concur in the ruling of the Grand Master in Decision N o. 12.
that the candidate's name must not appear on any such notice.
We move the adoption of the report, and recommend that it not be
printed in the California Masonic Code as it is cumulative.
Adopted unanimously.

minutes thereof.

DECISION NO. 15
The Grand Master ruled that the use of an ash tray embellished with
a Masonic emblem was in bad taste.
Under our law the following uses of Masonic emblems by Masons
are forbidden:
1. For advertising purposes.
2. For political purposes.
3. As th< name of any business not exclusively for Masonic purposes
(Sec. 333, 683 C.M.C.).
This Masonic law perforce applies to Masons only.
So limited, we recommend that the ruling be approved. Being
cumulative, it need not be published.
Adopted.
DECISION NO. 16
There was referred to the Committee on Jurisprudence the Grand
Master's Decision No. 16, being the question of whether a Lodge
may collect funds from its members and hold such funds in trust for
scholarship grants?
Section 405g C. M. C. provides that a Lodge may not act as Trustees
for individuals.
We concur in the Grand Master's decision that Lodges may not
collect funds from its members for such purpose but undP,r Section
409 C.M.C. Lodges may establish trust funds but only for purposes
which have direct connection with the business and welfare of the
particular Lodge and a trust fund for scholarship grants does not
operate for such purpose.
I move the adoption of the report.
Adopted.
DECISION NO. 18
There has been referred to the Committee on Jurisprudence Decision
No. 18 of the Grand Master, rendered on the following question:
"When the Master and both Wardens of a Lodge find it impossible for any of them to be present at an imminent Stated
Meeting of the Lodge. what course can be taken in order that
the necessary business of the Lodge may be disposed of?''
The Grand Master directed the Inspector of the District to be present
on the date of the Stated M eeting , that he preside at the meeting but
that the business be limited to the payment of current bills of the Lodge
and other business postponed to the next Stated Meeting.

DECISION NO. 7

At l : 30 p.m. Grand Lodge was called on. the Grand Master presiding.

Decision No. 7 holds that members of Job's Daughters ca nnot sell
tickets to a public event which entitle the purchaser to a chance to win
merchandise of value from $50.00 to $300.00 as a result of a drawing
by chance. Any such activity is in direct violation of Section 685-e of
our Masonic Code, and we concur with the Grand Master. (Not to be
recorded in the Code.)
Adopted.

COMBINED REPORTS OF
COMMITTEE ON JURISPRUDENCE
and
COMMITTEE ON POLICY AND GENERAL PURPOSES
(Items reported on at different times during the Communication are
con solidated to facilitate reference.)

DECISION NO. I
Decision No. 1 states that no fee may be paid to a brother as compensation for acting as Acting Master or Acting Chaplain at the funeral
of a deceased brother, except in the case of an ordained minister who
is requested to act as Acting Chaplain. Section 409 of the Masonic Code
covers the proper expenditures of Lodge funds. and Section 604 provides
that the Lodge may pay the burial expenses of a deceased brother who
dies in good standing and in financial circumstances requiring the Lodge
to pay this expense.
Your Committee concurs with the decision of the Grand Master but
wishes to point out that a brother should not expect to be compensated
for a Masonic duty and that any payment to an ordained minister must
be part of the burial expense of the deceased brother.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes concurred.
Adopted.

DECISION NO. 3
Decision No. 3 held that. in lieu of providing flowers for an ill brother
or paying the funeral expense of a deceased brother, a Lodge could not
contribute the cost of flowers to a Shrine Hospital. Section 411 of the
Masonic Code perm.its a contribution to the Masonic Homes Endowment Fund in lieu of flowers for a deceased brother if his family so
requests. but our law does not permit contributions of Lodge funds to
other organizations and we concur with the Grand Master. (Not to be
recorded in the Code. )
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes concurred.
Adopted.

DECISION NO. 9
Decision No. 9 holds that an application for affiliation could not be
received from one who received his Third Degree in a California Lodge
as a courtesy to another Grand Lodge then recognized by this Grand
Lodge but which Grand Lodge was not recognized by this Grand Lodge
when the application was presented to the Lodge. Section 319-a of the
Masonic Code provides that no application may be received under these
circumstances, and we concur with the Grand Master. (Not to be recorded in the Code. )
Adopted.

FUNERAL SERVICE LIMITAT ION
(B-4)
The Committee on Jurispruden ce:
Reporting on the resolution of Bro. Finley et al, we present the
following:
1. RESOLVE D : That the fourth sentence of Sec. 604 CMC be
repealed. Said sentence reads as follow s: "The Lodge may. in
its discretion , bury a member suspended for non-paymen t of dues
if there be no other Masonic offense established aga inst him ,
but it shall not pay the expenses of the burial.''
2. RESOLVE D: That Sec. 604-i CMC be repealed.
We move the adoption of the resolutions.
The C ommittee on Policy and General Purposes:
There has been referred to your Committee on Policy and General
Purposes a resolution which proposes to remove from our law the provision whereby a former M ason . suspended for non-paymen t of dues,
may, with approval of the Lodge of which he was once a member, be
buried with Masonic honors.
The elimina tion of this provision will ma ke our law clear and specific
that burial with Masonic honors is available only to Masons who are
in good standing. A former member who has been suspended for nonpayment of dues has available to him the opportunity and the procedure
for reinstatemen t. and had he himself desired to seek reinstatemen t he
would have done so prior to death. No pressure. occasioned by the
emotions of the family and friends at the time of the death of a former
Mason, can be placed upon the officers and members of a Lodge if this
provision is removed from our law, and thus there can be no decisions
made which might tend to bring discredit to M aso nry. We recommend a
"yes" vote.
The resolution w as not adopted.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 8 A. M . of California:
HISTORY RECOMMENDA TIONS
There has been referred to the Policy and General Purposes Committee that portion of the report of the Committee on Masonic History
recommending the assembling and compiling of a complete history of
Masonry in California for the ten year period from 1950 through 1960.
The history of Masonry prior to that time has been painstakingly
recorded and we feel that this work should be continued in order that
the story and romance of our fraternity may be handed down to future
generations accurately and as completely as possible.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes therefore recommends approval.
Adopted.

DECISION NO. 17
Decision No. 17 of the Grand Master's report, relative to the
propriety of Grand Lodge entering into a project to establish a home for
the aged, in which aged Masons, their wives and widows might be
cared for upon payment by them of amounts of money sufficient, or
more than sufficient to care for them during their lives, has been referred
to the Committee on Policy and General Purposes.
The Grand Master has ruled that it would be improper to enter
into such a project. and your Committee on Policy and General Purposes
concurs.
Adopted.

RESOL UTION ON INDEM NIFICA TION
A resolutio n on indemnification was referred at the last Commun ica.
tion of Grand Lodge to the Policy and General Purposes Committ ee
and was continue d to this Commun ication in order that your Committ ee
might have time to give the subject greater consider ation and study.
Your Committ ee feels that Grand Lodge should and would stand
by and defend its officers and committe emen against any legal action
that might be brought against them , if the action was caused by the
discharg e of their duties as officers or committe emen working on behalf
of Grand Lodge. but we feel that this resolutio n would be the issuance
of a blank check and would indemnif y an officer or committeeman
against any action that could be brought against them.
No limitation as to the amount of indemnif ication is placed in the
resolution, and it is entirely possible that action could be brought against
Grand Lodge for an exorbita nt amount because o f some action on the
part of officers or committe emen which would not be the responsib ility
of Grand Lodge.
.
Your Committ ee on Policy and General Purposes recomme
nds that
the resolutio n be not adopted.
The resolution was not adopted.

RECOM MEND ATION S COMM ITTEE ON RESEA RCH
The Committ ee on Policy and General Purposes has reviewed the
report of the Committ ee on Research which has been referred to us.
We are quite sympath etic with the aims and aspiratio ns of the Committee and commen d them for their zeal and imaginat ion.
It is our feeling. however , that all Committ ees, whether they be special or standing . should be under the control of the Grand Master and
subject to his screenin g. particula rly on the release of material bearing
the official imprint of the Grand Lodge.
It is our understa nding that the incoming Grand Master has made
plans to introduc e many innovatio ns and new procedur es relative to
Masonic Educatio n and Informat ion. Because of this, we are of the
opinion that no plan should be adopted at this time which would hamper
his program .
Further, we feel that the time is not yet here when the Committ ee
on Masonic Informat ion should have the status of a Standing Committee. Interest in Masonic Educatio n can be handled just as effectively
through the means of a Special Committ ee. In fact, a Special Committee is not limited in size, and the Grand Master has greater leeway
in the use of this type of Committ ee.
With these thoughts in mind. we recomme nd that the report of the
Committ ee on Research be flied without action.
Adopted .

jurisdictio n possess priceless Masonic historical objects, mementos ,

Because there are so many Lodges similarly blessed, whose members might also seek to have them declared M asonic Historical Monuments, your Committe e on Policy and General Purposes feels that

bers of the constituen t Lodges. The resolution has been referred to the
Finance C ommittee.
At a recent Annual Communic ation th is C ommittee unanimou sly opposed the adoption of a similar resolution . After the lapse of two yea rs
we see no reason to change our position. In fact. there is now a more
compelling reason to oppose it than existed at the time we last reported.
It became necessa ry last year to increase the per capita for the H omes
from 50 cents to $1.00, thereby raising the total per capita from $2.75
to $3.25. And it appears now tha t there can be no reduction this year.
It goes without saying that if you representa tives of the Lodges are
persuaded that there is sufficient merit in having all members receive the
magazine a t Grand Lodge expense - and the proposa l is not without
some merit - then you s hould vote in favor of the resolution .
H owever, in your considerat ion. we think yo u s hould keep in mind
that, if the resolution is adopted. it will mean the end of pa id su bscriptions. It will cost Grand Lodge in the neig hborhood of $100.000.0 0 per
year. And that means you and your Lodges, for the F inance Committee would have to ask you to add 40 cents to your per capita tax
for th is fiscal year . and each year hereafter. to foot this bill.
At the present time subscriber s totaling approxima tely 80.000 fall
into two main categories : those members w ho subscribe and pay for
the magazine directly; and those members for whom individual Lodges
subscribe and pay collectivel y.
To place our officia l magazine in the hands of all members is a fine
goal toward which to work. It would appear that we have made some
progress toward tha t goal on the present voluntary paid subscripti on
basis. We think further effort to expand this voluntary paid program
will build a sounder financial and circulation base than for Grand Lodge
to say. in effect, that it will req uire all Lodges to pay a per capita so
tha t the magazine may be sent to you free. We recommen d a "no" vote
on the resolution .

EARLY CALIFO RNIA LODGES
Your Committe e on Policy and General Purposes, having considered
the request of Harmony Lodge No. 164 that its temple be made a
Masonic Historical Monumen t, and having thoroughl y discussed the
importanc e of preserving the precious and priceless records. artifacts
and mementos of our early California Lodges, desires to strongly recommend to Grand Lodge that a Special Committe e be adopted by the
Grand Master to study and to recommen d to Grand Lodge means a nd
procedure s by which Grand Lodge may a id our early California Lodges,
when aid is needed. in the preservati on. safekeepin g and security of
the invaluable Masonic possession s to the end that they may not be
destroyed or lost and that they may be made available for the enlightenment and benefit of Masons in California for generation s to come.
Adopted.

AUDIT

"CALIFORNIA FREEMASON"

The firm of Skinner and Hammond. Certified Public Accountants.
has completed and furnished this Committee with copies of the audit
of the accounts of Grand Lodge and its agencies for the fiscal year
which ended June 30, 1960. We have examined these car~f ~lly and
discussed them with Brother Hammond and are of the opm1on that
they completely and accurately reflect the financial position ~f Grand
Lodge. As in the past, they are printed in the annual Pro~eedmgs .. We
recommend that you examine these at the first opportunity. It will be
time well spent.
The audit shows total revenue for the support of Grand Lodge of
$385,522.78, and expenses and appropriations of $327.337.80, leaving
a balance of unexpended revenue of $58.184 .98, which has been transferred to Capital Account.
It should be noted, however, that approximately $35,000.00 of this
surplus is represented by unexpended budget items wh~ch must be
budgeted again for the new fiscal year, as well as a net mcome from
the operations of "California Freemason" which should be transferred
to that reserve.

The audit report for the last fiscal year shows that cash receipts
from the publication of our official magazine, "California Freemason."
were in excess of cash disbursements in the amount of $7,449.43.
We recommend that Grand Lodge approve the appropriation of
$7.449.43 to be paid into "California Freemason Reserve." This will
bring the total amount in this reserve to $20,133.40.

GRAND TREASURER'S REPORT
The Grand Treasurer's report was referred to this Committee. Upon
examination we find all items to be in accord with the audit and we
recommend approval.

GRAND SECRETARY'S REPORT
There has been referred to this Committee that portion of the Grand
Secretary's report in which he recommends that certain Lodg e~ under
dispensation therein named be not required to pay the per capita tax.
We recommend approval.

EXCESS EXPENDITURES OVER BUDGETED AMOUNTS
There has been referred to this Committee that portion of the Grand
Master's message in which he reported approval by him of expenditures
in excess of budgeted items for the last fiscal year totaling $11.702 ..85.
The major portion of the excess is represented by one item for Retirement Pension Plan expense of $8,493.50 above the amounts budgeted
and appropriated. After the budget was approved it was found that
a higher percentage rate would be required for funding prior and current service credits for employees.
We recommend that this action by the Grand Master be approved.

It is estimated that approximately 232,000 individual issues of the
magazine have been subscribed for future issue. At 20 cents per copy
this makes a figure of $46,400.00. which represents our liability in this
respect. We should continue to build the reserve to an amount which
will offset our liability.

MASONIC HOMES
We have examined the audit of the accounts of the Masonic Homes
of California and have reviewed the report of the Trustees. In our
consultation with the Trustees we find that, where proper accounting
procedure and governing provisions allow, the Trustees are charging
certain maintenance and upkeep expense at the Homes to appropriate
reserves rather than to operating expense, thereby offsetting, to some
extent, the continuing rise in operating costs. Consequently, the Trustees
feel that a renewal of the Per Capita of $1.00 will be sufficient to support
their operating budget for the current fiscal year.
We, therefore, offer the following resolution:
"RESOLVED, that the sum of $1.00 per capita be levied
for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1961, the proceeds to be paid
to the Trustees of the Masonic Homes."
In submitting the budget for your consideration, we wish to make
special reference to several items.

NEW APPROPRIATIONS
In consultation with the Deputy Grand Master we discussed his
plans for the coming year which must be made in advance.
A new Special Committee on Masonic Information will be formed,
whose duties will be outlined at a later date. It is estimated that an
appropriation of $1,500.00 will be required, and it is included in the
budget.
The Library Comission will be asked to put into operation a special
program and will incur expenses in the estimated amount of $675.00,
which has been included in the budget.

PROCEEDING S OF THE

HISTORY COMMIT TEE
The History Committee has been asked to begin assembling the data
on Masonry in this jurisdiction in the decade which has elapsed since
the publication of " I 00 Years of Masonry in California." lt is estimated
that $3.000.00 will be required for this work in the current year. This
amount has been budgeted.
Your Finance Committee is in agreement that we should begin this
work without further delay. However, we feel that publication of any
supplement should be at greater intervals than ten years and recommend
that consideratio n by Grand Lodge of publication be reserved for such
time in the future as may be deemed most desirable.
RETIREM ENT PENSION PLAN
We are pleased to report that in the las t fiscal year the Retirement
Pension Plan became completely operative for Grand Lodge employees
and those of its agencies in the employ of the University Clubhouses,
Boards of Relief and Employeme nt Bureaus.
The full amount of past and current service costs for all pa rticipating
employees from the effective dates to the end of the fiscal year was paid
to the Trustee bank. For Grand Lodge purposes. payment to fund past
service costs is made at the required minimum rate of 2,Yi % of the total
of such services.
The details of these payments are listed in the audit report which
will be printed in the proceedings of this Communica tion.
For the current year our Actuarial Advisors estimate the cost of
direct employees to be $12,744.00, and of agency employees to be
$10,157.00. We have included these amounts in the budget.
MEMORI AL TEMPLE CA MPAIGN EXPENSE
On the recommenda tion of this C ommittee, Grand Lodge approved
the cost of the Open Book as a charge against the appropria tion for
Memorial T emple Campaign Expense. The entire appropriatio n was
not spent, as final bills were not rendered during the fiscal year.
We estimate that $8.500.00 will be required in the current year to
complete payment for this project and have included that amount in the
total appropriatio n of $10,000.00 for Temple Campaign Expense. The
remaining $1,500.00 is to cover incidental items of expense which may
occur from time to time.
Upon investigation , your Committee has concluded that Grand
Lodge will not be required to make further appropriatio ns for regular
and full ~time secretarial expense in the Memorial Temple Campaign for
voluntary contribution s and will be guided accordingly .

An examination of the annual budget for each of the last ten years
shows a fairly steady increase in the overall figu re. In view of the continued increase in the cost of all goods and services , it was to be expected that Grand Lodge would be and will continue to be faced with
this problem. F or example. in the budget which you have adopted , the
following items show increases over the previous year by these amounts:
Retirement Pension Plan - $11.900.00; Annual C ommunication $1 .000.00; Salaries - $16.400.00: Representatives' Mileage - $1.500.00; History Committee - $2.250.00. The Library Commission is
included for $675.00. and a new Special Committee on Masonic Information has been added for $1 .500.00. In addition to the above, there
are 9 separate items which have increased by $1 .000.00 or Jess for a
total of $5.750.00.
As against the above increases. we have been able to decrease only
3 items for a total of $7, 100.00.
In our efforts to eliminate any expense which would not contribute
directly to the efficiency of our operations and the support of the welfare and progress of Masonry in this jurisdiction, we have had the

280

GRAND LODGE O P CA L! P O RN IA

PROC EEDINGS OP THE

cooperation of the Chairmen of all Committees and Boards of Grand
Lodge and those in charge of administration .
However. we must all take a realistic view of risin g costs. Grand
Lodge is only as strong as the constituent Lodges. It would seem to
be advisable for each Lodge to re-examine its financial position in the
light of increased cost of operation and , where it appears necessary,
give consideration to an increase in member dues .
The estimated s urplus of $I .257.50 is much less than an amount
which would be considered desirable. normally. and provides no margin
for any emergencies which may arise; but if proper care is exercised in
spending Grand Lodge funds. we are of the opinion that estimated
income s hould suffice and that no increase in per capita is required.
W e. therefore. off er the following resolution:

Grand Lodge. a per capita aggregating $3.25 be levied for the

PROCEEDING S OP T HE

PHILIPPIN E GAVELS
The Grand Secretary directed the attention of Grand Lodge to a
gift from the Grand Lodge of the Philippines. presented by Brother
Honoria M. Saycon of Kasilawan Lodge No. 77. The gift consisted
of gavels for the Grand Master, the Senior Grand Warden and the
Junior Grand W arden, all made of narra wood, the national tree of
the Philippine Islands. The gift of a gavel of sim ila r wood was made
personally to the Grand Secretary by Brother Saycon.
Grand Master Joe L. Shell made an appropriate speech of acceptance on behalf of the Grand Lodge of California.

ANNUAL ELECTIO N
The Grand M aster announced that th e hour had arrived for the
Annual Election a nd directed the Grand Secretary to read the Sections
of the Constitution applying to the sa me.
